description: Machine-readable evidence for the Web Fleet browser Audit network boundary. Audit is a manual, operator-triggered browser evaluation. The hard requirement is that Chromium cannot resolve or navigate to any destination the Go process would have rejected, because Chromium owns its own networking. Evidence lives in internal/audit/proxy_test.go, internal/audit/browser_test.go and internal/audit/proc_unix.go.

architecture.proxy: An in-process GuardedProxy listens on 127.0.0.1 and is passed to Chromium via --proxy-server with --proxy-bypass-list=<-loopback>, so even loopback traffic flows through the proxy. Chromium never resolves or dials the target itself; it hands the hostname to the proxy.
architecture.validation: Every CONNECT and absolute-form HTTP request through the proxy is validated by the same netguard public-network guard used by monitoring and crawling (scheme http/https only; resolved addresses must be public).
architecture.dialTimeRecheck: Every dial-time resolution set is validated in full before any address from that set is connected: the guarded dialer rejects an empty answer, normalizes/unmaps all addresses, fails closed if the set contains any blocked address regardless of answer ordering, and only then dials the allowed addresses with multi-address fallback. A DNS rebinding that hides a private address behind a public one is therefore unusable even if the public address appears first.
architecture.redirects: The proxy never follows redirects. Chromium follows them itself, and each redirect hop is a fresh proxied request that is validated again.
architecture.prevalidation: The target URL is also validated before the browser launches as a fast-fail and defense-in-depth check.
architecture.sandbox: Chromium runs with its own OS sandbox by default (WEBFLEET_AUDIT_SANDBOX=strict, no --no-sandbox). --no-sandbox is only used when the operator explicitly sets WEBFLEET_AUDIT_SANDBOX=allow-no-sandbox, documented as a downgrade for environments that cannot sandbox Chromium.
architecture.processLifecycle: The browser runs in its own process group; on timeout or cancellation the whole tree is SIGKILLed (proc_unix.go) so renderers are not orphaned.
architecture.bounds: Per-audit execution timeout (45s default), bounded DOM output (16MiB) and stderr (1MiB), and a global audit concurrency semaphore (2) that bounds simultaneous browser processes including batch audits.

blockedDestinations: alternate numeric/hex/octal IP forms that do not resolve to a canonical public address

tested.case: CONNECT to loopback/private/link-local/reserved/documentation/cloud-metadata (169.254.169.254) and IPv6 forms returns 403
resolver returns a public address for validation then a private address at dial; the connection is refused

netguard shared boundary: a dial-time answer set containing any blocked address ([public,private], [private,public], v6/v4 mixes, IPv4-mapped private, link-local/unique-local/documentation) is denied before any address in the set is dialed, independent of answer ordering
validation sees an all-public answer, the dial-time answer is mixed; the connection is refused
an empty dial-time answer set is refused
after the full set passes validation, multi-address fallback across allowed addresses still works
proxy returns a 302 without following it, and a follow-up CONNECT to the private redirect target is refused
non-http schemes and origin-form requests are refused
absolute-form HTTP is validated and forwarded

REAL Chromium: the target hostname resolves only through the injected proxy resolver; the fixture is reached, proving Chromium routed through the guarded proxy (a bypass would leave it unable to fetch)
loopback target is refused before launch under the production guard
a hung upstream cannot exceed the per-audit timeout and is not reported as success
browser DOM output is bounded and excess output is consumed without blocking the child
the global audit semaphore allows exactly two concurrent browser audits
audits only run on explicit request and history defaults off
strict sandbox never passes --no-sandbox; allow-no-sandbox is explicit opt-in

knownBehavior: Chromium performs background connectivity probes (e.g. CONNECT www.google.com:443) through the guarded proxy. They are validated like any other request: public destinations pass, private/unresolvable ones are refused. Audit therefore requires the host to reach the public internet; operators should expect these probes.
Batch audits run at the same global concurrency as single audits and are org-filtered by the route layer; a batch can therefore take a long time but cannot exhaust the process.

manualAndHistory.evidence: Audit runs only from the explicit POST /api/sites/{id}/audit and /api/audits/batch routes (permission audit.run); no scheduler or crawler path invokes the audit runner. audit_settings.history_enabled defaults to 0 and is only flipped by the operator.
